sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Cobb County?
sections.html:
County and school taxes arrive in one bill from the Cobb County Tax Commissioner, who collects for the Board of Commissioners and the school district. A parcel outside city limits stops there. A parcel in Acworth, Austell, Kennesaw, Mableton, Marietta, Smyrna or Powder Springs also gets a city bill, since each of those seven cities collects for itself.

Values are not the commissioner's call. Each year the Board of Tax Assessors sets fair market value, and Georgia taxes 40% of it. The overview page writes the formula as (Fair Market Value x 0.40) x (Millage Rate / 1,000), where one mill is $1 per $1,000 of assessed value. County, school and city authorities choose their rates annually.

The 2026 digest produced 270,574 bills worth $1,363,609,369, according to the county's announcement. Real property accounted for 256,894 of them and personal property for 13,680. Eligible homesteads also received the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant for 2026, which appears as a reduction on the bill apart from any exemption.

sections.h2: When is Cobb County property tax due?
sections.html:
Bills go out by August 15 and fall due October 15. Collection cannot start until the tax digest is approved, normally in mid to late July, so nobody can prepay. The 2026 bills were issued in mid August and were due October 15, 2026.

Money is on time if the office has it, or if the envelope bears a Postal Service postmark dated by midnight on October 15. Meter and kiosk stamps do not count. A bill that has not shown up by August 30 can be printed from the commissioner's website, and its absence does not excuse penalty or interest.

The office takes partial payments, yet whatever remains after October 15 is charged a 5% penalty and monthly interest. Arrangements start with a call to 770-528-8600. A returned check costs $30 or 5%, whichever is greater, plus bank charges.

sections.h2: Where and how can you pay a Cobb County tax bill?
sections.html:
Owners can pay online by e-check or card, call 1-866-535-2622, mail a check to P.O. Box 100127, Marietta, GA 30061, or walk in. Drop boxes sit at several offices. The e-check route has no convenience fee, and the county says it keeps none of the card fees.

Escrow accounts work like this: once a lender tells the office it pays your taxes, the bill goes to both of you, and you remain responsible for confirming it was paid. A double payment is refunded. The coupon is optional as long as the parcel ID is written on the check.

sections.h2: What if I disagree with my Cobb County valuation?
sections.html:
A value dispute is filed in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice date, and the commissioner has no say. The grounds are value, uniformity and taxability, never the millage rate. Cases the assessors do not resolve go on to the Board of Equalization.

Filing an appeal does not move the due date. The bill for a parcel under appeal carries a lower appeal amount, set at 85% of assessed value or 100% of the prior uncontested value, and at least that much must be paid by October 15 to avoid the 5% penalty. Interest of up to $150 a month can accrue on the remainder; paying the full bill by the due date avoids it.

The commissioner's 2026 estimator runs on 2025 millage rates and covers county tax alone, leaving out city tax and special classifications. A second version for new home buyers lets you enter a market value, a tax district and exemptions. Whatever it shows, the official bill controls.

sections.h2: What homestead exemptions and relief can a Cobb County owner use?
sections.html:
The basic homestead exemption goes to owners living in the house as their primary residence on January 1. Seniors can claim more starting at age 62, including a full or reduced school tax exemption. Other exemptions cover 100% service-connected disabled veterans, disabled owners, surviving spouses of certain public servants, nonprofits and religious organizations.

File online, in person or by mail, with the application received or postmarked before the appeal deadline on your assessment notice. Anything later is processed for the next year. If you held an exemption elsewhere, include a letter showing it was removed. A rental cannot carry a homestead, and an owner who keeps one after becoming ineligible owes penalties and interest on the taxes saved.

A marriage, divorce, death or ownership change calls for a fresh application backed by a recorded deed, marriage certificate or divorce decree. Special classifications such as conservation use, historic property and forest land go through the assessors.

sections.h2: What happens when Cobb County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Once the due date passes, the office sends a written notice, and 30 days later it may issue a Fi. Fa., a tax execution that works as a lien. The Fi. Fa. brings a $23 charge on taxes under $100 or $33 on taxes over $100, plus administrative costs. Late fees are never waived.

A sale takes place on the first Tuesday of any month where one is scheduled, at Superior Court Plaza on the corner of Haynes Street and Washington Avenue. Bidding runs from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., in person only, after pre-registration, and winners pay with cash or a certified check. What is sold is the tax deed, never a tax lien. Redemption stays open for 12 months, and the price adds the bid, any later taxes the buyer paid, special assessments, and a premium of 20% for the first year or fraction and 10% for each year after.

  • Get a written payoff before listing.
  • A filed Fi. Fa. adds its fee to the payoff.
  • After a tax sale, redemption stays open for 12 months.

sections.h2: How are Cobb County taxes handled when you sell?
sections.html:
Proration is not something the commissioner does. A full year of tax is figured on the parcel, responsibility is sorted out when the sale closes, and your closing paperwork says who pays. The tax follows the property, so whoever owns it at the time should make sure it is paid.

Afterward, report the ownership change to the commissioner and have your homestead exemption removed. The new owner files for theirs under the rules above. A house with tenants, repairs or a delinquent bill can still move, and the payoff comes out of proceeds either way.

faqs.q: What date do Cobb County property taxes come due?
faqs.a: October 15, with bills mailed by August 15. The 2026 bills fell due October 15, 2026. A payment counts if it arrives or is postmarked by the Postal Service by then, and what is left afterward draws a 5% penalty plus monthly interest.

faqs.q: Does Cobb County allow installment payments?
faqs.a: Partial payments are taken, and interest and penalty still build on the balance after October 15. Arrange payments by calling 770-528-8600. An appeal does not defer payment, though only the appeal amount is required by the due date.

faqs.q: Will Cobb County split the tax bill between me and the buyer?
faqs.a: No, the office stays out of it. The bill covers the whole year, and your closing paperwork decides each side's share. The closing attorney or title company usually pays from proceeds.

faqs.q: What if my Cobb County tax bill never arrived?
faqs.a: The tax is still owed, and penalty and interest stand. Print the bill from the commissioner's website, pay with the parcel ID on your check, or call 770-528-8600. A corrected mailing address prevents a repeat.

faqs.q: How long can an owner redeem after a Cobb County tax sale?
faqs.a: Twelve months from the sale. The owner, a creditor or anyone else with an interest may redeem by paying the bid, later taxes, special assessments and the stepped premium of 20% then 10%. The buyer calculates the exact figure.
